title: ASR Source Profile (source.json)
description: The operational profile of one authoritative source: what it is, why it is trusted, what it holds, how it is reached, and what evidence backs each access claim. A profile is a living document — probes update its verification blocks, humans update its adjudication and guidance — but it must never overstate: an access method's verification.state is DERIVED from probe records (§04), and machine-asserted authority is quarantined from human-adjudicated authority. What a source holds (content) and how it is reached (access) are separate blocks by design.

source_id.description: Content-addressed: "asc\n" + canonical_url (§06). Deliberately NOT UPC's src- prefix: an ASR source is a service profile, a UPC source is a captured object.

name.description: The source's common name; the slug is computed from it (§06).

publisher.description: The operating legal/organizational entity, when distinct from name.

homepage_url.description: The public front door as given.

canonical_url.description: homepage_url normalized by the §06 URL algorithm; feeds identity. A changed canonical_url is a NEW source related by supersedes.

authority.description: Why this source is trusted — in two quarantined halves. `asserted` may be written by a machine at add-time and is triage, not judgment. `adjudicated` is the human scoring pass: its tier/score are null until a person (or an explicitly attributed process) fills them, and the validator requires attribution when they are non-null (adjudication_unattributed) and warns when the profile's provenance says a model wrote it (adjudication_by_machine). Consumers that need one number use adjudicated.tier ?? asserted.tier and must preserve the distinction when re-exporting.

asserted_by.description: Who/what made the triage call, e.g. "authority add" or a model id.

tier.description: Human-confirmed tier on the same 1/2/3 scale; null until adjudicated.

score.description: Optional finer-grained score in [0,1]; null until adjudicated.

method.description: How the adjudication was made (rubric name, review process).

topics.description: Topic ids; every entry MUST exist in the registry's topics.json (unknown_topic).

notes.description: Free text for compound realities ("Federal 9th Circuit ruling scoped to CA").

coverage_start.description: ISO date or year the content coverage begins.

coverage_end.description: ISO date, year, or the string "present".

content.description: WHAT the source holds — deliberately separate from access. artifacts describe the kinds of objects; landing_pattern records how many hops from a public URL to the artifact you actually want (the "report landing page" problem made explicit).

formats.description: File/wire formats as lowercase extensions or MIME-ish names, e.g. ["pdf"], ["json", "csv"].

access.description: Every viable way in, ordered by preference (first = try first). Each method's verification block is governed by the hard promise: state derives from probe records, never from optimism.

verification.description: Source-level rollup: the WORST state among access methods, ordered broken > blocked > stale > asserted > degraded > verified (retired methods are excluded from the rollup). Recomputed by regen/validate; stored for browsability.

guidance.description: The token-frugal payload for agents: what this source is best for, query shapes that actually work, and pitfalls that waste round-trips. Render this FIRST in human views too — it is the payoff of the profile.

task.description: The research task this shape serves.

access.description: access method name this recipe runs against; null when the shape is not method-specific.

endpoint.description: endpoint name within that access method, when applicable.

recipe.description: How to shape the query/request, in imperative prose.

llm_notes.description: Anything else an agent should know before spending requests.

cadence_notes.description: Free text for what the enum cannot say ("updated as filed", "annual each October").

effective_date.description: For sources whose content takes force on a date (standards, statutes).

target.description: Either an in-registry reference (source_id) or an external pointer (name + url) for sources not yet profiled.

discovery.description: How this source entered the registry — discovery provenance, kept because a registry is also a record of research method.

retrieved_via.description: The exact query or session action that surfaced it, verbatim.

import_ref.description: Id in the corpus this was imported from, e.g. "FORGE-2B-017"; null when not an import.

ext.description: Tool-namespaced extension data. ext["pi-forge"] conventionally carries {provider, kinds, selectors} for the export crosswalk.

access_method.description: One way into the source. auth carries a credential REFERENCE only — a secret value in any tracked file is the credential_in_profile error. robots posture is recorded per method because different transports sit under different paths and rules.

name.description: CLI-addressable slug, unique within the profile.

credential_ref.description: Registry-unique slug the resolution chain (§05) looks up. Convention: name it after the pi-forge provider id when one exists, so FORGE_API_KEY_<REF> resolves with zero mapping.

location.description: Where an api_key travels; required when scheme is api_key_query or api_key_header.

name.description: The parameter or header name, e.g. "api_key" or "x-ebirdapitoken".

signup_url.description: Where a human obtains a key.

limits.description: Declared or observed politeness limits; enforced by probe/fetch and exported to consumer budget ledgers. Absent fields mean unknown, not unlimited.

politeness_delay_ms.description: Overrides the registry default when set.

daily_budget.description: Requests per day, when the provider declares or meters one.

applies.description: Whether robots.txt governs this transport (false for authenticated APIs, ftp, offline).

posture.description: null = not yet recorded (an L1 error where robots applies — probe to fill).

checked_path.description: The path whose allowance was evaluated.

tos_url.description: Terms-of-service URL, recorded as metadata; never auto-fetched.

verification.description: The access claim this method makes, governed by the hard promise: state is DERIVED from probes.jsonl (§04). Stored here as a cache for browsability; disagreement with derivation is state_drift.

last_verified_at.description: Timestamp of the last ok probe; null when never verified.

window_days.description: Per-method staleness override; null uses the registry default.

endpoint.description: An operational recipe under an access method: enough detail that an agent (or `authority fetch`) can execute it without reading external docs. path_template uses {param} placeholders resolved from params[] and --param flags; the credential placeholder is injected by the auth block, never written into the template.

name.description: CLI-addressable slug, unique within the access method.

path_template.description: Path + query template relative to base_url, with {param} placeholders, e.g. "/v2/electricity/retail-sales/data?frequency={frequency}".

type.description: Informal type hint: string, integer, date, enum:..., etc.

cursor_path.description: JSON path to the next-cursor/token in the response, for cursor/token styles.

record_path.description: JSON path (dot notation) to the records array within a structured response, e.g. "response.data".

probe_hint.description: The cheapest real invocation of this endpoint, used by `authority probe` as the API ping. For OAI-PMH the convention is the Identify verb.

example_request.description: A ready-to-read example URL or request line with $CREDENTIAL placeholders where a secret would go.
